outline.chapter_title: Introduction: The Bottlenecks of Modern Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter explores the current state of Large Language Models (LLMs) and the practical challenges associated with their deployment, specifically focusing on computational and environmental costs.
subtopics: The rise of LLMs and their multi-modal capabilities
Hardware limitations: Memory bandwidth and power constraints
The environmental and economic impact of high-precision (FP16/BF16) training and inference
Current solutions: Post-training quantization (PTQ) and its limitations
The motivation for training-aware low-bit architectures

outline.chapter_title: The 1-bit Paradigm: From Floating-Point to Integer Arithmetic
outline.description: This chapter introduces the fundamental shift from standard floating-point matrix multiplications to the 1-bit computation paradigm popularized by BitNet.
subtopics: The dominance of matrix multiplication in Transformer architectures
Computational costs of floating-point addition vs. multiplication
The BitNet concept: Replacing nn.Linear with BitLinear
Energy efficiency gains in integer-based computation
Memory footprint reduction: DRAM-to-SRAM transfer efficiency

outline.chapter_title: Technical Deep Dive: The BitNet b1.58 Architecture
outline.description: This chapter details the specific technical innovations that define BitNet b1.58, including its unique quantization methods and structural components.
subtopics: Defining 1.58-bit: The ternary weight system {-1, 0, 1}
Weight Quantization: The absmean function and RoundClip mechanism
Activation Quantization: 8-bit scaling and zero-point removal
LLaMA-alike components: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, and Rotary Embedding (RoPE)
Design choices: Removing biases for software compatibility (Huggingface, llama.cpp)

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Evaluation: Performance and Scaling Laws
outline.description: This chapter analyzes the experimental results of BitNet b1.58 compared to full-precision LLaMA models, focusing on accuracy, speed, and resource consumption.
subtopics: Benchmarking methodology: RedPajama dataset and zero-shot task evaluation
Perplexity and End-task performance parity at the 3B scale
Comparative analysis: Latency, GPU memory usage, and throughput
The new scaling law: Equivalent model sizes between 1.58-bit and 16-bit models
Energy analysis: Savings in arithmetic operations on 7nm chips

outline.chapter_title: The Future of 1-bit AI: Edge, MoE, and Hardware
outline.description: The final chapter discusses the broader implications of 1.58-bit LLMs for the future of the AI industry, including hardware specialization and mobile deployment.
subtopics: Enabling 1-bit Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) for reduced inter-chip overhead
Native support for long sequences and KV cache compression
Deploying LLMs on Edge and Mobile devices: Overcoming memory constraints
CPU-friendly computation and the need for specialized 1-bit hardware (LPUs)
Conclusion: A new recipe for the next generation of LLMs
